subject: toucan
pitch: A keel-billed toucan showing off on a short mossy branch. A huge rainbow beak in lime green, sky blue and orange with a cherry-red tip, a glossy black body, a lemon-yellow bib, a ring of lime-green skin around each eye, bright blue feet and a scarlet patch under the tail. A single pink orchid blooms on the branch beside it.
reasoning:
I'm planning the scale for the toucan model, roughly 0.5m long with a sizeable beak, perched on a short mossy branch resting near ground level.

I'm sketching the layout: a horizontal branch supported by a stump reaching the ground, with the toucan body as a scaled ellipsoid facing forward, a tail extending backward, and an orchid attached further along the branch.

For the head, I'm adding a sphere with a textured eye ring, dark pupil, and then the signature oversized beak built from tapered cylinder segments colored lime green, sky blue, and orange with a cherry-red tip, flattened and curved to mimic a keel-billed toucan's shape. Next I'm working on the lemon-yellow bib across the chest.

Now I'm setting up bright blue legs and gripping toes wrapped over the branch, glossy black folded wings along the body sides, moss patches scattered on the branch and stump, and a small pink orchid with magenta-centered petals perched nearby on the branch.

Writing build function code...

Building the branch and stump geometry...

Adjusting body position so legs connect naturally to the branch, then working out the tail geometry with a slight downward rotation so it droops realistically at the back end.

I'm adding a small red patch beneath the tail base as a child of the tail mesh, positioning it in local tail coordinates near the body side. Then I'm placing the head sphere on top of the body and starting on the beak position extending forward from the head.

For the beak, I'm building cylindrical segments along Y and rotating them 90° around X so they point forward in Z, keeping radiusTop as the front tip and radiusBottom as the back base, then scaling the mesh to make the beak cross-section taller than wide to match a keel-billed toucan's profile.

Defining beak segments...

I'm skipping extra beak ridge details for budget and moving to eye placement, adding small ring accents around the eyes using torus geometry oriented to face outward, with a green-toned skin color for the eye rings.

I'm positioning the bib as a flattened sphere wedged between the chest and head, then building the folded black wings as flattened ellipsoids on each side of the body, keeping the overall shape simple while skipping any extra yellow markings.

Now I'm adding thin blue cylindrical legs with box-shaped toes, sizing the branch so the feet rest naturally on top of it. For the orchid, I'm planning a curved tube stem rising from the branch to a bloom made of radial petal ellipsoids with a magenta lip, yellow center, and a couple of small pink buds along the stem.

I'm working out petal placement using angular rotation around the flower's center so each ellipsoid points outward correctly, then adding scattered moss patches along the branch and a soft green mound at the base of the stump for ground cover.

Now I'm checking overall proportions—height, branch length, and orientation so the toucan faces forward with its beak pointing out—before moving into writing the actual Three.js scene setup, starting with a seeded random helper and the module metadata.

Now I'm placing the eyes with rings, pupils, and highlights symmetrically on each side of the head, then starting on the leg cylinders positioned below the body.

Working out the toe and foot placement so they sit flush on the branch surface, then shifting to the orchid flower geometry—building the bent stem curve, petal ellipsoids arranged radially with a distinct larger dorsal petal and magenta lip, plus small buds and leaves attached near the base. I'm planning to use a CatmullRomCurve3 with TubeGeometry for the stem and typed Vector3 points, then finalize the full code with proper TypeScript types before presenting it.
